package_info.package_name: Unknown (multiple npm packages targeted via hijacked S3 buckets)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (depends on which packages had S3-hosted assets hijacked)
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers are leveraging expired AWS S3 buckets previously used by legitimate npm packages to inject malicious code into the supply chain, allowing them to compromise users without modifying the original package codebase.

execution_context.trigger: import-time/runtime (whenever the package loads remote assets)
execution_context.file_location: Remote asset URL in package code (e.g., JavaScript referencing S3 bucket)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code loads and executes a remote JavaScript file from a hijacked S3 bucket, allowing arbitrary code execution in the context of the application.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading and executing remote code from an external, now-uncontrolled S3 bucket is a classic supply chain attack vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not load code from expired or untrusted remote sources, especially after asset ownership changes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use might include loading assets from a trusted CDN or the package author's own S3 bucket, but only if the bucket is properly secured and maintained.
key_indicators: References to expired or recently-registered S3 buckets
Dynamic script injection from external sources
No code changes in the npm package itself, but new behavior observed

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers or takes over an expired S3 bucket previously referenced by a legitimate npm package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to serve arbitrary content from the hijacked bucket

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is uploaded to the hijacked S3 bucket.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now available at the original asset URL

attack_chain.action: When users install or run the npm package, their application loads and executes the malicious code from the hijacked S3 bucket.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution in user environments

behavioral_signatures: Dynamic script injection from external S3 buckets
Unexpected network requests to S3 buckets not controlled by the package author
Execution of code loaded from remote, non-CDN sources
file_indicators: References to S3 buckets in package source code or asset URLs
Changes in remote asset content without corresponding package updates
network_indicators: Requests to S3 buckets with recently changed or suspicious ownership
Loading of JavaScript from S3 buckets not previously associated with the package
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that reference external S3 buckets, especially those with expired or recently-registered domains. Flag dynamic script injection patterns and alert on network requests to S3 buckets that have changed ownership or are not associated with the original package author. Compare remote asset content hashes over time to detect unauthorized changes.
